note: Opening-line formulas for LinkedIn posts. The first line has to work on its own: mobile cuts the preview at roughly 140 characters. Pick by what the idea actually is, never by habit. Examples are illustrations only; never reuse their numbers as if they were the user's.
rules: The hook is one line, alone, with a blank line under it.
Line two pays off line one. It is not more setup.
A hook must be true for this user. If it needs a number they have not given, ask for it.
Three options from three different formulas, never three versions of one.

hooks.name: Contrarian
hooks.template: {Common advice} is wrong. Here's what worked instead.
hooks.example: Posting every day was the worst thing I did for my reach.
hooks.use_when: The user holds a real position against the default advice in their field.
hooks.ruined_by: Picking a fight with a strawman nobody actually believes.

hooks.name: Before / After
hooks.template: {Time} ago I {old state}. Today I {new state}.
hooks.example: Last spring our support queue was 3 days behind. This week it hit zero by Tuesday.
hooks.use_when: There is a measurable change and the user knows what caused it.
hooks.ruined_by: Skipping the middle. The post is the how, not the glow-up.

hooks.name: Owned Mistake
hooks.template: I {did something wrong} and it cost {specific cost}.
hooks.example: I hired for culture fit and lost a quarter to it.
hooks.use_when: The user made a mistake they can name and price.
hooks.ruined_by: A humble-brag dressed as a mistake ('my flaw is I care too much').

hooks.name: The Number
hooks.template: {Surprising number}. {What it means in five words}.
hooks.example: 71 cold emails. 2 replies. Both from the subject line I almost cut.
hooks.use_when: One figure carries the whole story.
hooks.ruined_by: A vanity metric with no context, or a number the user can't back up.

hooks.name: Specific List
hooks.template: {N} things I {learned/changed/stopped} after {specific experience}:
hooks.example: 4 things I stopped doing after running 60 interviews in one month:
hooks.use_when: The lessons are genuinely separate and each one stands alone.
hooks.ruined_by: Generic tools or tips anyone could list. The experience is the hook, not the list.

hooks.name: Overheard Line
hooks.template: "{Something someone actually said}"
hooks.example: "We don't need a process, we need fewer meetings." - our newest engineer, day 3.
hooks.use_when: A real quote triggered the idea.
hooks.ruined_by: Invented dialogue. If nobody said it, don't quote it.

hooks.name: Question Nobody Asks
hooks.template: Why does nobody {question about an accepted practice}?
hooks.example: Why do we interview for 5 hours and onboard for 30 minutes?
hooks.use_when: The user has noticed a real gap in how things are done.
hooks.ruined_by: A question with an obvious answer, or one the post never answers.

hooks.name: Scene
hooks.template: {Time and place}. {What happened, in one plain sentence}.
hooks.example: Friday, 6:40pm. Our biggest client emailed asking for the contract termination clause.
hooks.use_when: There is a story with a moment of tension.
hooks.ruined_by: Starting with backstory instead of the moment.

hooks.name: Unpopular Admission
hooks.template: I {do something people are told not to}, and I'm not stopping.
hooks.example: I still reply to every recruiter, even when I'm not looking.
hooks.use_when: The user has a habit that cuts against advice and a reason for it.
hooks.ruined_by: Fake rebellion. It has to be something that really draws pushback.

hooks.name: Cost of Waiting
hooks.template: I waited {time} to {do the thing}. It cost me {cost}.
hooks.example: I waited two years to raise prices. That was roughly 30% of revenue left on the table.
hooks.use_when: Delay had a measurable cost.
hooks.ruined_by: No real cost stated. Without the cost, there is no post.

hooks.name: Side by Side
hooks.template: {Option A} vs {Option B}. {Which won, unexpectedly}.
hooks.example: A paid course vs a weekend reading the docs. The docs won.
hooks.use_when: The user compared two things directly.
hooks.ruined_by: A comparison where the winner is obvious from the start.

hooks.name: Rule I Follow
hooks.template: My one rule for {situation}: {rule}.
hooks.example: My one rule for code review: never leave a comment I wouldn't say out loud.
hooks.use_when: The user has a short principle they actually apply.
hooks.ruined_by: A platitude. If no one would disagree, it's not a rule worth a post.

hooks.name: Behind the Number
hooks.template: {Impressive result}. Here's the unglamorous part.
hooks.example: We closed our biggest deal this year. It took 14 months and 3 lost champions.
hooks.use_when: A win has a messy story behind it.
hooks.ruined_by: Turning the unglamorous part into another flex.

hooks.name: Prediction
hooks.template: In {timeframe}, {specific prediction}. Here's why.
hooks.example: By 2028, most job applications will be read by an agent before a person.
hooks.use_when: The user has a reasoned, specific view about where their field is going.
hooks.ruined_by: Vague futurism. Name a date and something checkable.

hooks.name: Small Change, Big Effect
hooks.template: One {tiny change} {big result}.
hooks.example: Moving our standup from 9:00 to 11:30 cut 'quick sync' meetings in half.
hooks.use_when: A minor tweak had an outsized result.
hooks.ruined_by: Overclaiming causation. Say what else changed too.

hooks.name: Advice I Ignored
hooks.template: Someone told me {advice}. I ignored it for {time}. They were right.
hooks.example: My first manager told me to write things down. I ignored it for 6 years.
hooks.use_when: The user learned something late and can say what it cost.
hooks.ruined_by: No consequence. The gap between ignoring and learning is the post.

hooks.name: Time Compression
hooks.template: {Task} used to take {long time}. Now it takes {short time}.
hooks.example: Month-end reporting used to take me two days. Now it's 40 minutes.
hooks.use_when: There is a real, measured speed-up and the user can explain how.
hooks.ruined_by: Numbers that look made up. Round, believable figures beat dramatic ones.

hooks.name: The Ask I Got
hooks.template: A {role} asked me {question}. My answer surprised them.
hooks.example: A new grad asked me how to get promoted. I told them to stop asking.
hooks.use_when: Someone asked the user a real question worth answering publicly.
hooks.ruined_by: A made-up question, or an answer that isn't surprising.

hooks.name: Walk Away
hooks.template: I said no to {something attractive}. Here's why.
hooks.example: I turned down a 30% raise last month.
hooks.use_when: The user declined something most people would take.
hooks.ruined_by: Virtue signalling. Give the real reasoning, including the doubt.

hooks.name: Myth Check
hooks.template: Everyone says {belief}. The data I have says {different thing}.
hooks.example: Everyone says Tuesdays are the best day to post. My last 40 posts say it doesn't matter.
hooks.use_when: The user has their own data that contradicts a common belief.
hooks.ruined_by: Too small a sample presented as proof. State the n.

hooks.name: Give It Away
hooks.template: Here's the {template/checklist/script} I use for {task}. Take it.
hooks.example: Here's the 5-line email I send when a deal goes quiet. Copy it.
hooks.use_when: The user has a reusable asset and is willing to share it in full.
hooks.ruined_by: Gating it behind 'comment YES and I'll DM you'. Put it in the post.
